Testimony in Support of LD 1629: "An Act to Require Legislative Committees to Provide Equal Time to
Each Member of the Public Who Testifies"
Senator Baldacci, Representative Salisbury, and the distinguished members of the Committee on State and Local Government, my name is Harris Van Pate and I serve as policy analyst for Maine Policy Institute. Maine Policy is a free-market think tank, a nonpartisan, non-profit organization that advocates for individual liberty and economic freedom in Maine. Thank you for the opportunity to provide testimony supporting LD 1629, "An Act to Require Legislative Committees to Provide Equal Time to Each Member of the Public Who Testifies."
At its core, LD 1629 promotes a simple yet profound principle: equality in public discourse. In a representative democracy, the Legislature must strive to provide equal opportunity for citizen engagement, especially during public hearings--the very forum where the voices of Maine people are most directly heard. This bill ensures that each Mainer, regardless of background, organizational affiliation, or political persuasion, is granted the same opportunity to participate in the legislative process.
LD 1629 helps by mandating that legislative committees give equal time to all members of the public who testify during public hearings. This does not stifle debate--it strengthens it by upholding the principles of fairness and transparency. As every citizen has one vote, each should be entitled to an equal voice in public testimony.
Some may argue that this will make hearings less efficient. We disagree. A commitment to fairness may require more careful scheduling or time limits across the board, but efficiency must never come at the cost of democratic integrity or civic engagement. Legislators are stewards of the public trust, and part of that responsibility is ensuring that all voices are welcomed and heard on equal footing.
Further, this bill aligns with Maine's long-standing tradition of citizen engagement and participatory government. It embodies Maine Policy Institute's belief that government should serve the people, not special interests, and that policy decisions should be grounded in an open, inclusive process.
We urge the committee to vote "Ought to Pass" on LD 1629. By ensuring equal time for all testifiers, the Legislature affirms its commitment to a fairer, more transparent, and more accountable process for all Mainers. Thank you for your time and consideration.

Senator Baldacci, Representative Salisbury, and esteemed members of the State & Local
Committee Thank you for the opportunity to present my bill, LD 1629: "An Act to
Require Legislative Committees to Provide Equal Time to Each Member of the Public Who Testifies"
Those who were here last session may remember LD 1619. I am not discussing the bill
itself, but only want to speak to what I feel was the absolute disrespect shown to members of the public who waited hours to testify. Before the hearing began, members of the public were notified that they had three minutes of time in which to give their testimony and that it would be timed. All of the supporters of the bill were given the three minutes that was advertised. As the day wore on and opponents were testifying, that time was abruptly changed to two minutes. I watched as members of the public, who had taken
the day off of work, driven for hours and then waited for hours, scramble to re-write their
testimonies. Many people were upset. As they should be. They were being denied the opportunity to have their voices heard equally. You can imagine how others felt, when
later, they were told that they would only be permitted one minute in which to testify after having already changed their testimonies from three minutes to two minutes and waiting for well over 12 hours. Once again, they scrambled to change their testimonies. This time, only being allowed to testify for 1/3 of the time that all the proponents of the bill were given and that they were told they would be given. There was no equity or
equality in this building for that hearing.
It was disgraceful and should never happen again, regardless of if you are for or against a bill. It was the process that was so heinous. Is a person more important earlier in the day?
Is one person's testimony more valued than another's? Do supporters of a bill deserve better treatment than those who oppose a bill? Once again, this is not about the bill, but rather the contempt and disregard that was shown to people who had driven, some of
them for hours, to have their voices heard on a bill. Their voices were cut short and they were not afforded the same opportunity that others were given.
I have had constituents tell me that they are not going to waste their time again to be so readily dismissed. They were truly disenfranchised. They know they were not being
listened to. They found it difficult to even attempt to make their point in a minute when
